title: Countable-dimensional modules over the continuous endomorphism algebra are reconstructed from a rank-one corner
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite with its extended norm [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $V\ne0$ be a normed $E$-vector space and fix an algebraic basis $(b_j)_{j\in J}$ (every vector has a unique finite linear expansion), with $0\in J$, where $J=\{0,\ldots,d-1\}$ for some $d\geq1$ or $J=\mathbf N$. Suppose constants $0<c\leq C<\infty$ bound the norm of every finite linear combination between $c\max_j|a_j|$ and $C\max_j|a_j|$. Give $V$ its norm topology. Let $D=\operatorname{End}^{\mathrm{cts}}_E(V)$ be the unital $E$-algebra of all continuous $E$-linear endomorphisms, with multiplication given by composition. Write $\lambda_0:V\to E$ for the $b_0$-coordinate and $e(v)=\lambda_0(v)b_0$, a continuous idempotent of rank one. If $H$ is any unital left $D$-module whose induced $E$-vector space is algebraically spanned by at most countably many elements, put $eH=\{eh:h\in H\}$. Then the specified map
$$V\otimes_E eH\longrightarrow H,\qquad v\otimes h\longmapsto \theta_v h,\qquad\theta_v(w)=\lambda_0(w)v,$$
is an isomorphism of left $D$-modules, where $D$ acts on the first tensor factor. No topology or continuity assumption is imposed on $H$. The assertion includes $H=0$ and finite-dimensional $V$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent coefficient auxiliary: rank-one reconstruction using the finite-rank ideal and an uncountable almost-disjoint family of coordinate subsets. Exact reference WANTED; intended proof in report.md.

proof.text: Write $\lambda_j$ for the coordinate of $b_j$. The lower bound gives $|\lambda_j(v)|\leq c^{-1}\|v\|$, so each coordinate is continuous. For every $i,j\in J$ the operator $E_{ij}(v)=\lambda_j(v)b_i$ satisfies $\|E_{ij}(v)\|\leq (C/c)\|v\|$, hence belongs to $D$. Checking basis vectors gives $E_{ij}E_{kl}=\delta_{jk}E_{il}$ and $e=E_{00}$. Also $\theta_v(w)=\lambda_0(w)v$ has $\|\theta_v(w)\|\leq c^{-1}\|v\|\|w\|$ and is continuous. These estimates use finite algebraic expansions only.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent coefficient auxiliary: rank-one reconstruction, explicit coordinate calculation.

proof.text: Since $e^2=e$, its image $eH$ is an $E$-subspace and $eh=h$ for $h\in eH$. The function $(v,h)\mapsto\theta_vh$ is $E$-bilinear, because $v\mapsto\theta_v$ is $E$-linear and the $E$-action on $H$ comes from the central scalar operators in $D$. It therefore induces the specified linear map $\Phi:V\otimes_E eH\to H$. For $T\in D$, evaluation on $w$ gives $T\theta_v(w)=\lambda_0(w)T(v)=\theta_{T(v)}(w)$. Thus $\Phi(Tv\otimes h)=T\Phi(v\otimes h)$, proving $D$-linearity.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent coefficient auxiliary: rank-one reconstruction, explicit coordinate calculation.

proof.text: To prove injectivity, expand the first factors of any tensor using the algebraic basis and collect terms: $z=\sum_{j\in F}b_j\otimes h_j$ for a finite $F\subseteq J$ and $h_j\in eH$. If $\Phi(z)=\sum_{j\in F}E_{j0}h_j=0$, apply $E_{0k}$ for each $k\in F$. The matrix-unit identities give $0=eh_k=h_k$. Hence $z=0$. No independence theorem for tensor products is required, only bilinearity and the finite expansions.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent coefficient auxiliary: rank-one reconstruction, explicit coordinate calculation.

proof.text: Put $N=\operatorname{im}\Phi=\{\sum_{r=1}^n\theta_{v_r}h_r:n\geq0,\ v_r\in V,\ h_r\in eH\}$. The preceding $D$-linearity makes $N$ a $D$-submodule, so $Q=H/N$ is a unital $D$-module. It is countably spanned over $E$: project the given countable spanning family of $H$ to $Q$. For every $h\in H$, $eh=\theta_{b_0}(eh)$ lies in $N$, so $eQ=0$. Consequently $E_{jj}=E_{j0}eE_{0j}$ acts as zero on $Q$. If $J$ is finite, $1_D=\sum_{j\in J}E_{jj}$, whence $Q=0$. It remains to prove $Q=0$ when $J=\mathbf N$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent coefficient auxiliary: rank-one reconstruction, explicit coordinate calculation.

proof.text: Assume now $J=\mathbf N$. Apply [lem-sfb-uncountable-almost-disjoint-family] to obtain an uncountable index set $I$ and infinite subsets $A_i\subseteq\mathbf N$ with finite pairwise intersections. For each $i$, let $a_i:\mathbf N\to A_i$ enumerate $A_i$ in increasing order. This enumeration exists by successively taking the least element not yet listed: infinitely many elements ensure each next choice, and an element $m\in A_i$ must occur among the first $m+1$ choices. Thus $a_i$ is a bijection.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent coefficient auxiliary: infinite-coordinate case, almost-disjoint-family input.

proof.text: For $i\in I$, define $u_i(b_n)=b_{a_i(n)}$ and define $r_i(b_{a_i(n)})=b_n$, with $r_i(b_m)=0$ for $m\notin A_i$. Extend by finite linear combinations. Reindexing preserves the maximum of the nonzero coefficients; deleting coordinates cannot increase it. The two norm bounds therefore give $\|u_i(v)\|\leq(C/c)\|v\|$ and $\|r_i(v)\|\leq(C/c)\|v\|$. Both maps belong to $D$. On basis vectors $r_iu_i=1_D$ and $u_ir_i=p_i$, where $p_i$ keeps precisely the coordinates in $A_i$. In particular $p_i^2=p_i$ and $p_iu_i=u_i$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent coefficient auxiliary: rank-one reconstruction, explicit coordinate calculation.

proof.text: For distinct $i,j$, put $F=A_i\cap A_j$, a finite set by step 5. Computing on each basis vector gives $p_ip_j=\sum_{k\in F}E_{kk}=\sum_{k\in F}E_{k0}eE_{0k}$. Since $e$ annihilates $Q$, this product annihilates $Q$. This uses only finite coordinate projections, and needs no identification of all continuous finite-rank operators with a generated ideal.

proof.text: Let $W\subseteq Q$ be the image of a countable spanning set of $H$, so $W$ is countable and spans $Q$. Apply [lem-sfb-independent-family-spanning-cardinality] with $K=E$, $M=Q$ and the independent family of step 8. It supplies an injection $I\to W$. Composing with an injection $W\to\mathbf N$ contradicts the uncountability of $I$. Therefore $Q=0$ also for infinite $J$.

proof.text: In either case $Q=H/N=0$, hence $N=H$ and $\Phi$ is surjective. Together with step 3 this makes $\Phi$ a bijective $E$-linear and $D$-linear map. Its inverse is $D$-linear as well: if $y=\Phi(z)$, then $\Phi(Tz)=Ty$, so uniqueness of the preimage gives $\Phi^{-1}(Ty)=Tz$. This is precisely the claimed isomorphism with the given action on the first tensor factor. If $H=0$, both tensor product and target are zero and the same argument applies; finite-dimensional $V$, including $d=1$, was handled in step 4.
